title: Reported speech
examples: How do I change 'I am going' to reported speech?
Do I always change the tense when I report what someone said?
What happens to words like 'here' and 'now'?

explain.say: Today we are learning to report what someone said. This is called reported speech. It means we are telling someone else about a conversation.
First we look at backshifting the tense. When we change from direct to reported speech, we often move the verb tense back. This is called backshifting.
For example, if someone says "I like pizza," we change it to "She said she liked pizza." Notice the change from like to liked.
Next we change pronouns and time words. We must change words like 'I' to reflect who is speaking now. We also change 'today' to 'that day'.
Let us practice with a full sentence. If John says "I will finish this tomorrow," we report it as "John said he would finish that the next day." Remember to adjust everything.

items: Reported: He said he would leave the next day.

draw.text: John said he would finish that the next day.

explain.say: In real life, you use this when retelling a story. For example, if a friend tells you, "I bought this today," you can report it as "My friend said she bought that day." You are passing on information.

faq.q: Do I always have to change the tense?
faq.a: No, you do not always have to change the tense. If the statement is a general truth, you can keep the original tense.
asks: Must I change the verb tense?
When can I keep the original tense?

faq.q: What if the original statement is about a permanent fact?
faq.a: If the statement is a permanent fact, like 'The Earth is round,' you usually do not need to change the tense.
asks: Is it okay to keep the tense for facts?

faq.q: How do I change 'now' to reported speech?
faq.a: You change 'now' to 'then' or 'at that time.' This helps the listener understand when the event happened.
asks: Can I use 'then' for time words?

faq.a: Yes, 'here' usually changes to 'there.' This is part of changing time and place references.
asks: What is the word for 'here' in reported speech?

faq.q: What if the reporting verb is in the past tense?
faq.a: If the reporting verb, like 'said,' is in the past, you generally need to backshift the tense of the reported speech.
asks: If I use 'told,' what do I do next?
Does the reporting verb control the tense change?

facts: When reporting speech, the tense of the verb often moves back into the past.
Words indicating time, such as 'today' and 'now,' must usually change.
Pronouns like 'I' and 'you' must change to reflect the new speaker's perspective.
If the original statement is a universal truth, the tense change can sometimes be avoided.

quiz.say: Direct: "I have finished my homework."; Reported:
quiz.show: She said she had finished her homework.

options.show: She said she finished her homework.
options.say: She said she finished her homework.

options.show: She said I had finished my homework.
options.say: She said I had finished my homework.

options.show: She said she had finished her homework.
options.say: She said she had finished her homework.

options.show: She said she has finished her homework.
options.say: She said she has finished her homework.

quiz.why: The present perfect tense 'have finished' correctly shifts back to the past perfect 'had finished'.

wrong.0: This changes it to the simple past, which is a common mistake when backshifting.
wrong.1: This incorrectly changes the pronoun 'I' to 'I' instead of a third-person pronoun.
wrong.3: This keeps the tense in the present, which is incorrect when reporting speech in the past.

quiz.say: Direct: "We are at the park now."; Reported:
quiz.show: They said they were at the park then.

options.show: They said they were at the park now.
options.say: They said they were at the park now.

options.show: They said they were at the park.
options.say: They said they were at the park.

options.show: They said they were at the park today.
options.say: They said they were at the park today.

options.show: They said they were at the park then.
options.say: They said they were at the park then.

quiz.why: The tense 'are' shifts to 'were,' and the time word 'now' correctly shifts to 'then.'

wrong.0: Keeping 'now' is wrong because the reporting is happening later.
wrong.1: Omitting the time change makes the report less precise.
wrong.2: This incorrectly changes the time word 'now' to 'today'.

quiz.say: Direct: "I will call you tomorrow."; Reported:
quiz.show: He said he would call me the next day.

options.show: He said he would call me the next day.
options.say: He said he would call me the next day.

options.show: He said he will call me tomorrow.
options.say: He said he will call me tomorrow.

options.show: He said he would call me tomorrow.
options.say: He said he would call me tomorrow.

options.show: He said I would call me the next day.
options.say: He said I would call me the next day.

quiz.why: The modal 'will' changes to 'would,' 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day,' and 'you' changes to 'me' based on context.

wrong.1: Keeping 'will' is wrong because the reporting verb is in the past.
wrong.2: Keeping 'tomorrow' is wrong because time expressions must shift.
wrong.3: This incorrectly changes the pronoun 'I' to 'I' and 'you' to 'me'.
